## Example 3.7 · Create and compare {#l2-example-3-7-graphs .compact}

**Part 2: Creating the graphs**

a) Select **Score, Frequency (Bar), Frequency (Line)**.
b) Insert a **Combo Chart**: columns for the histogram and a line for the polygon.
c) Select **Score** and both **Relative Freq** columns (Ctrl, or Cmd on Mac, for non-adjacent columns).
d) Insert a second **Combo Chart**.

**Part 3: Analysis**

a) What do you notice about the shapes of the two graphs?
b) How do their vertical-axis scales differ?
c) Explain mathematically why the shapes remain identical.
<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 43 · Example 3.7 · Complete the working in your booklet.</p>

::: notes
Retains all Part2 and Part3 tasks. Spreadsheet menus differ by app/version. Format columns to touch (zero gap width where supported); otherwise identify the result as a column-chart approximation to a histogram. The prescribed polygon convention also requires zero-frequency endpoints one class beyond each end: here x=0 and x=6. Add these helper rows when the charting app needs explicit endpoints. The booklet dataset itself is unchanged. Total32 means rf=f/32, a uniform rescaling.
:::
